text:
Gabriel Vilardi is the Jet whose chances haven't turned into goals yet. He has three goals on 7.4 expected (the quality of his chances), shooting 6.5% against a range for him around 15%. Nothing about how he plays suggests that lasts: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 9.4 scoring chances per 60 from the home-plate area in front of the net last season, 99th percentile among forwards, and he is often on the end of passes across the slot, which go in far more often than other shots.

It's a slow start after a strong 2025-26, when Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.4 wins, 34th among forwards, with a knack for drawing penalties. He's no skater by NHL Edge (bottom 5% in top speed); he wins his ice around the net instead.

The signs are turning. His minutes are up nearly three a night over the last 10 games, he had a three-point night with the late equalizer in Chicago, and seven of his 14 points have come on the power play. Watch the goals catch up to the looks.
